findings.evidence: "This workspace holds 3 projects, synced last week." followed by a list with only two `<li>` entries ("Data Warehouse Cutover", "Mobile App Revamp")
findings.fix: Either add the missing third project to the list or change the copy to clarify this is a partial/recent list (e.g., "Recent projects" with a "View all 3" link).
findings.violation: The stated project count (3) doesn't match the number of projects actually listed (2), with no indication that the list is partial.

findings.fix: Wrap each project name in an anchor/button that links to that project's own settings or detail view.
findings.violation: The project names are plain text with no link or button, so there is no way to navigate into either specific project from the overview.

findings.evidence: "Invite 3 teammates this month to unlock the advanced reporting add-on."
findings.fix: Add a call-to-action link (e.g., to the invite flow) and/or a progress indicator ("1 of 3 invited").
findings.violation: The promo text has no accompanying link, button, or progress indicator, giving the user no way to act on it or see how many invites they've already sent.

findings.evidence: The overview link is simply labeled "Open project settings" (not tied to any project), yet the destination form is pre-filled with `value="Design System Refresh"`, a project that isn't one of the two listed in the overview.
findings.fix: Either scope the link per-project (e.g., one settings link per list item) or make clear in the overview which project "Open project settings" refers to.
findings.violation: There is no project-selection step, so it's unclear which project's settings are being opened, and the hardcoded project name is inconsistent with the projects shown on the overview page.

findings.fix: Add label text such as "Duplicate project" inside the button (or an `aria-label` if it must stay icon-only).
findings.violation: The button has no visible text or accessible label, so users can't tell what it does.

findings.evidence: `<button id="project-settings-save-btn" type="submit">Save</button>` with no subsequent confirmation step
findings.fix: Add a confirmation state or message after saving, consistent with the other flows.
findings.violation: Unlike the invite and archive flows (which lead to "Invite sent" / "Project archived" confirmation screens), saving project settings gives no feedback that the save succeeded.

findings.evidence: `<input id="project-settings-name-input" type="text" value="Design System Refresh">` has no `name` attribute
findings.fix: Add appropriate `name` attributes to all form inputs and selects.
findings.violation: Without `name` attributes, these form fields would not be submitted as data when the form posts.

findings.evidence: A `` inside the form, plus a separate `Continue` outside it
findings.fix: Combine into a single action (e.g., the Save button itself navigates to "Invite sent" on submit), removing the redundant Continue link.
findings.violation: It's unclear whether "Save" or "Continue" is what actually sends the invite - having both suggests two competing triggers for the same action, which is confusing.

findings.evidence: "An invite was sent to the address entered above."
findings.fix: Display the actual email address that was invited on the confirmation screen instead of referring back to a field that's no longer visible.
findings.violation: This is a separate section from the invite form, so the "address entered above" is not actually visible or carried over anywhere on this page - the reference is unverifiable to the user.

findings.evidence: "You can restore it at any time from the archived projects list." / "It no longer appears in the active projects list for anyone on the team."
findings.fix: Add an archived-projects section (with a restore action) and link to it from these messages, or remove the claim if out of scope.
findings.violation: Both sections reference an "archived projects list" page, but no such section or link exists anywhere in the document.

findings.evidence: `<select id="notification-settings-digest-input"><option>Daily</option><option>Weekly</option></select>` with no `selected` attribute on either option
findings.fix: Mark the option matching the current saved setting with `selected`.
findings.violation: The settings form doesn't reflect the user's actual current digest preference, defaulting ambiguously to the first option.

findings.evidence: `<button id="notification-settings-save-btn" type="submit">Save</button>` with no resulting confirmation
findings.fix: Add a save-confirmation message or redirect to a confirmation state.
findings.violation: As with project settings, saving here gives no feedback that the change was applied, inconsistent with the invite/archive flows' confirmation screens.
